issues.failure_explanation: Three bound inaccuracies in the net-extension step. (i) The rows of A = (1/sqrt(m)) A_1 bullet ... bullet A_d are (1/sqrt(m)) times a Kronecker product of unit-variance vectors; applying the cited proposition with t = n^{d/2} to the unnormalized rows controls only P(max_i ||a_i||^2 > 4 n^d/m) <= 2m e^{-cn/d}, whereas E_1 is defined with the smaller threshold 2 n^d/m, so the displayed probability bound for E_1 does not follow from the stated step (it is recovered with t = (sqrt(2)-1) n^{d/2}, same order 2m e^{-c'n/d}). (ii) In the final union bound the cross term is written 2 sqrt(1+delta) sqrt(2 n^d/m) eps, but the derivation gives 2 sqrt(1+delta) sqrt(2 n^d) eps; with the correct term the event is still empty for eps = delta n^{-d/2}/3 (total <= 14 delta/9 < 2 delta), so the conclusion is unaffected. (iii) The bound ||A^x x - A^{xhat} xhat||^2 <= m ||A x - A xhat||_infty^2 is justified via a lemma for signed order statistics, while trimming selects rows by absolute value; sign changes of the retained order statistics are not controlled by the cited lemma and require a short additional argument (a sign flip at rank j forces ||A(x-xhat)||_infty to be comparable to the retained value).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Control E_1 using t = (sqrt(2)-1) n^{d/2} (or a Bernstein lower-tail bound for the row norms), correct the cross term to 2 sqrt(1+delta) sqrt(2 n^d) eps, and add one short paragraph justifying the comparison of trimmed vectors under absolute-value sorting; no change to the statement, rates, or sample complexity.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the paper's main trimming theorem is not valid as written at the net-extension step. The theorem statement, the sample complexities in \eqref{eq:order_m_hosvd} and \eqref{eq:order_m_cp}, and the probability 1 - c n^{-phi} are all preserved by the local repairs; no downstream formal result is invalidated since the statement is unchanged.
issues.title: Net-extension step of the trimmed TensorRIP proof contains bound inaccuracies
issues.why_classification: All three defects are local bound inaccuracies within a single proof step; each repair is a constant adjustment or one short paragraph, and the theorem's statement, sample complexity, and probability guarantee survive unchanged, so the least adequate complete resolution is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Then, the $j$-th row of the trimmed matrix $\mat{A}_k^\vx \in \R^{ (m - k) \times n}$  is given by
$$ \sqrt\frac{{m}}{m-k} \va_{i_j} \quad j \in [m-k]\;.$$

Note that, in the noiseless case $(\eta = 0)$, the trimmed matrix at iteration $k$, $\mat{A}_k$ corresponds to $\mat{A}_{m_{trim}}^{\algoname{Vec}(\tX^k - \tX^*)}$ as per Definition~\ref{def:trimmed-matrix}.
with a sufficiently large $m$ and $m_{trim} \approx \ln(8n)$ ensures that with high probability $| 1 - \Delta_t| < \delta$ for any $t$.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm selects the m_trim rows with smallest |A(X^k) - b| and scales the gradient by m/|Theta_k| = m/m_trim, i.e., it keeps m_trim rows and drops m - m_trim rows. The analyzed trimming (Definition def:trimmed-matrix, Theorem theorem:trim_trip) drops only k = ln(8 n^phi) rows and keeps the m - k smallest. Consequently: (i) the rescaled matrix in the displayed equation uses sqrt(m/(m - m_trim)), but consistency with Step 5 and |Theta_k| = m_trim requires sqrt(m/m_trim); (ii) the claimed identity of A_k with A^{Vec(X^k - X*)}_{m_trim} is false, since that object keeps m - m_trim rows, not m_trim; (iii) with the reported experimental range m_trim in {5,...,80} out of m about 2700-4250, the implemented algorithm discards over 95% of the measurements, far outside the regime of Theorem theorem:trim_trip, so the RIP-based justification of the implemented TrimTIHT is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change Step 4 of Algorithm alg:trimtiht to keep the m - m_trim smallest-residual rows (Theta_k = [i_1, ..., i_{m - m_trim}]), which simultaneously fixes the rescaling equation, the correspondence to Definition def:trimmed-matrix, and the applicability of Theorem theorem:trim_trip with m_trim ~ ln(8n); the empirical m_trim tuning must then be re-run under this convention.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central link -- TrimTIHT implements the trimming that Theorem theorem:trim_trip shows restores norm preservation -- is false as printed. The parameter guidance m_trim ~ ln(8n) in Remark rem:trimtiht-discussion and the reported experimental tuning follow the opposite convention, and the theoretical guarantee does not cover the procedure actually implemented.
issues.title: TrimTIHT keeps the wrong rows: the algorithm's trimming convention contradicts the analyzed trimming
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the algorithm restores full consistency with the definition, the scaling identity, and the main theorem, so no new proof architecture is needed and the main result survives; however, the repair changes the procedure's actual operation and invalidates the reported experimental tuning, which must be re-optimized, so the resolution is more than minor.

issues.failure_explanation: The contraction factor depends on t through mu_t, rho_t, Delta_t, xi_t, and the proof establishes only the one-step inequality ||R^{t+1}|| <= alpha_t ||R^t||. Iteration yields ||R^{t+1}|| <= (prod_{s<=t} alpha_s) ||R^0||, which is not bounded by alpha_t^{t+1} ||R^0|| unless alpha_s <= alpha_t for all s <= t; e.g., alpha_0 = 0.9, alpha_1 = 0.1 gives the true bound 0.09 ||R^0|| versus the claimed 0.01 ||R^0||. The statement as written is therefore unsupported by the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the conclusion as the proved one-step bound ||R^{t+1}||_F <= alpha_t ||R^t||_F, or as the product bound ||R^T||_F <= (prod_{t<T} alpha_t) ||R^0||_F.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's stated convergence form (a power of a time-dependent factor times the initial error) is not established; the per-step contraction and the discussion in Remark rem:trimtiht-discussion, which explicitly uses the one-step form, survive.
issues.title: thm:main_path states an iterated bound with a time-dependent factor that its one-step proof does not establish
issues.why_classification: The proof is correct for the one-step bound and the stated iterated form is repaired by a pure restatement; no method, rate, or advertised scope is lost, so a short local repair suffices.

issues.failure_explanation: The simplification of \eqref{eqn:conv_path} to \eqref{eqn:conv_path_err} requires sqrt(2 xi_t + xi_t^2) (1 + mu_t ||A_t||_2 sqrt(Delta_t)) <= |1 - mu_t Delta_t|, i.e., with c_t := |1 - mu_t Delta_t| / (1 + mu_t ||A_t||_2 sqrt(Delta_t)), the condition xi_t <= sqrt(1 + c_t^2) - 1, which is approximately c_t^2/2 for small c_t. The stated hypothesis permits xi_t up to (16/17) c_t^2 ≈ 0.94 c_t^2; e.g., c_t = 0.9 and xi_t = 0.76 give sqrt(2 xi_t + xi_t^2) ≈ 1.45 > c_t. So the condition is insufficient by nearly a factor of two, and the simplified bound on which the delta < 0.106 TIHT-recovery claim and the trimming implications for rho_t rest is not established as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant 16/17 by a valid one, e.g., require xi_t <= |1 - mu_t Delta_t|^2 / (2 (1 + mu_t ||A_t||_2 sqrt(Delta_t))^2 + |1 - mu_t Delta_t|^2) (equivalently xi_t <= sqrt(1+c_t^2)-1), or directly assume sqrt(2 xi_t + xi_t^2)(1 + mu_t ||A_t||_2 sqrt(Delta_t)) <= |1 - mu_t Delta_t|; the delta < 0.106 analysis is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified contraction bound \eqref{eqn:conv_path_err} and the conclusions built on it (recovery of the TIHT guarantee for delta < 0.106 and the trimming discussion for rho_t) rest on an insufficient hypothesis; all of these conclusions survive after a constant-factor correction of the condition.
issues.title: Sufficient condition on xi_t in the TrimTIHT discussion does not imply the simplified contraction bound
issues.why_classification: The hypothesis is wrong only by a constant factor; replacing 16/17 by a valid constant (or stating the required domination directly) restores the simplified bound and all downstream discussion without any new argument or loss of content.
